name: Isolated Focal Cortical Dysplasia Type Ib

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: International League Against Epilepsy (ILAE) Classification of Focal Cortical Dysplasia

criteria.description: Presence of isolated cortical dyslamination without dysmorphic neurons or balloon cells on histopathological examination
MRI evidence of focal cortical thickening or blurring of the gray-white matter junction consistent with focal cortical dysplasia
Focal epilepsy with seizures often refractory to medical treatment
EEG showing focal epileptiform discharges corresponding to the lesion location

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of isolated cortical dyslamination plus clinical and imaging evidence of focal epilepsy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires surgical tissue sampling; MRI findings may be subtle or negative in some cases.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal onset seizures with impaired awareness
Epileptogenic zone localized to cortical dysplasia area
searchTerms: seizure area matches brain cortex abnormality
seizure focus in dysplastic brain area

common.symptomName: Aura with sensory or autonomic features
searchTerms: aura with sensory or automatic symptoms
pre-seizure sensations involving senses or body functions
sensory or autonomic warning before seizure

common.symptomName: Cognitive impairment related to seizure burden
searchTerms: memory and learning issues related to seizures

occasional.symptomName: Mood disturbances including anxiety or depression

searchTerms: weakness on one side of body from seizures
partial paralysis related to seizure focus
loss of part of the vision field
blind spots or missing areas in vision

imaging: MRI showing focal cortical thickening, blurring of gray-white matter junction, or transmantle sign
PET scan may show focal hypometabolism in affected cortex
genetic: Somatic mutations in mTOR pathway genes reported in some cases
other: Histopathology demonstrating isolated cortical dyslamination without dysmorphic neurons or balloon cells

distinguishingFeatures: Multisystem involvement with skin, renal, and pulmonary lesions
Presence of cortical tubers and subependymal nodules on imaging
Genetic mutations in TSC1 or TSC2 genes
Histopathology shows dysmorphic neurons and balloon cells
More prominent MRI abnormalities including transmantle sign

redFlags: MRI-negative epilepsy with clinical suspicion of cortical dysplasia
references: Blumcke I, et al. The clinicopathologic spectrum of focal cortical dysplasias: a consensus classification proposed by an ad hoc Task Force of the ILAE Diagnostic Methods Commission. Epilepsia. 2011.
Fauser S, et al. Clinical characteristics of patients with focal cortical dysplasia type I and II. Epilepsia. 2006.
